title: Rotation heatmap, incident digest, and handoff — Apr 21 2027
content:
Purpose and audience:
This note captures the SRE rotation heatmap from the last 7 days, short incident digests, SLO signals that crossed thresholds, and explicit on-call handoff items for the next shift. Intended for on-call engineers, SRE leads, and platform owners.

Highlights (one-liner):
- Traffic spike + backend cache regression (Incident A) was the highest-severity event; mitigated by targeted cache purge & fallback policy.
- Two lower-sev degradations traced to misrouted model variants and a queued retry storm.
- Heatmap shows persistent late-evening latency blips across us-west-2 for long-sequence chat workloads.

Metrics snapshot (7d):
- Error budget remaining (global request SLO 99.7%): 93.4% (used 6.6%).
- Median p95 tail latency (text-gen): 210ms; p99: 1.2s (spikes during 02:00-04:00 UTC).
- Autoscale events: 4 manual scaleouts, 11 autoscale cycles; two failed scale attempts (see JIRA-1430).

Incident digests (concise):
1) Incident A — cache-regression + traffic spike — Apr 19 09:12–10:35 UTC
- Symptom: sudden 5–8x increase in per-request token compute times; elevated p99 and increased queueing in front of runtime nodes.
- Root cause hypothesis: regression introduced in cache invalidation path in nightly deploy (PR 788) that caused frequent cache misses for common prefixes; amplified by a small client-side retry loop.
- Mitigation applied: roll back PR 788 in staged fleet, targeted prefix cache warm (warm keys replay), temporarily enable per-customer relaxed batching for affected tenants.
- Postmortem notes: create a canary test for cache miss rate, add a metric alert on cache hit ratio delta > 15% within 10m. Owner: Samira Khan (action: JIRA-1428).

2) Incident B — model-variant misrouting — Apr 20 02:41–03:08 UTC
- Symptom: 0.6% of requests routed to a debug build of a model that has longer init times, causing transient high tail latency.
- Root cause: incomplete routing table upload during a partial rollout; control-plane retry logic replayed an older mapping under load.
- Mitigation: roll-forward to the correct mapping, temporarily increase retry jitter to avoid synchronized retries.
- Follow-up: harden rollout mapping validation; add a preflight probe that checks cold-start latency. Owner: Diego Alvarez.

3) Incident C — queued retry storm (low-sev) — Apr 17 23:05–23:45 UTC
- Symptom: downstream service returned 503s leading to client retries queuing at gateway and transient slowdown.
- Mitigation: raised client-side backoff policy and drained queues via controlled drain.
- Long-term: investigate client retry policy defaults and publish recommended SDK backoff settings. Owner: Morgan Patel.

Heatmap findings (new visualization summary):
- Pattern: recurring 02:00–04:30 UTC latency tail elevation concentrated in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Heatmap correlates spikes with long-conversation (>2048 tokens) distributions.
- Hypothesis: kernel choice for longer sequences yields lower throughput at those times due to co-located GPUs reaching burst thermal throttling on lower-utilization nodes.
- Short experiments to run: (a) schedule a daytime-only test of sequence-sampling workload on reserved nodes, (b) swap kernel variant to alternate quantized path for a subset (small canary). Lead: Avery Chen.

SLO and alert changes recommended:
- Add alert: cache-hit-ratio-drop > 12% over 5m with simultaneous p99 > 800ms. Rationale: catches cache regression earlier.
- Adjust existing scaling alert: trigger an on-call paging only if scale repeated 3x in 15m (reduces noise for transient bursts).
- Introduce synthetic long-convo probe that runs every 15m from multiple regions and reports cold-start time and generation tail latency.

On-call handoff (explicit items for incoming shift):
- Primary: watch for cache-hit-ratio alert; if fired, check recent deploys (tags) and if related to PR 788 rollbacks, coordinate with runtime on-call.
- Secondary: ensure rollout mappings report healthy; check control-plane upload logs for mapping upload errors (grep controlplane:upload in logs).
- Triage checklist: confirm p99 generator latency trimmed, confirm no queued-retry > 1000 requests, clear any prolonged autoscale failures.
- Contact points: @samira (runtime), @diego (routing), @morgan (gateway). Slack channel: #sre-bridge (pinned: Apr21-rotation-debrief).

Action items (owner / due):
- Samira: add cache-hit-ratio delta alert + create canary that simulates common prefixes (due 2027-05-03).
- Diego: rollout mapping preflight probe + stronger upload validation (due 2027-05-05).
- Morgan: publish SDK recommended backoff note and patch default retry jitter (due 2027-04-29).
- Avery: run the kernel-swap canary and report performance delta in next stability sync (due 2027-04-27).

Runbook edits proposed (short):
- Add a "cache regression" page: checklist to quickly determine whether elevated latency is cache-hit related, steps to perform safe prefix-warm, and rollback guidance.
- Add a "mapping rollback" table with explicit mapping to control-plane logs and rollback commands.

Meeting and notes:
- This doc was reviewed in the 2027-04-21 SRE sync (attendance: Avery, Samira, Morgan, Diego, and guest: Lina from runtime infra). Lina emphasized adding a metric for per-tenant miss amplification.

Risks/notes for PMs and Product owners:
- If cache miss amplification is not addressed, cost per token could materially increase due to repeated recomputation—estimate up to +12% GPU-hours for affected tenants. Consider gating high-cost workloads behind dedicated capacity if SLA-critical.

Next check-in:
- Quick status update on action items due Apr 27 (kernel canary) and Apr 29 (SDK backoff). Full postmortem for Incident A to be filed once root cause is confirmed; draft expected by May 5.

Raw references and commands:
- Example log query: project=runtime severity>=warn "cache-miss" | window 10m | top(50)
- Control-plane upload debug: curl -XPOST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/mapping/validate -d '{"mapping":...}'

If anything is unclear in these notes ping me (Avery) or update the doc directly.
